entertainment.title: How The One Ring Helps Sauron Control The Other Rings Of Power
entertainment.summary: "The Rings of Power" season 3 finale shows but a glimpse of the One Ring's immense power, leaving us with a lot to look forward to in season 4.
entertainment.body:
New Line Cinema Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 – "The Doom of Men"

"The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 sees Sauron finally wielding his One Ring of power — that is, until he takes it off and surrenders to his enemies. Don't worry, there's more to that move than the Dark Lord willingly giving up. He'll be back. When Sauron first forges the One Ring at the end of Episode 7 , he puts it on, and the Elven ring-bearers immediately remove their own overpowered jewelry. They're aware of the Dark Lord, and they don't want to be controlled by him. But what exactly does the One Ring do to allow the Dark Lord to control the other Rings of Power?

Tolkien doesn't give a clear, scientific answer here. But in "The Silmarillion" he does provide a good summary: "Now the Elves made many rings; but secretly Sauron made One Ring to rule all the others, and their power was bound up with it, to be subject wholly to it and to last only so long as it too should last." The book explains that Sauron pours much of his own strength and will into his Ring so it can control the others, saying, "while he wore the One Ring, he could perceive all the things that were done by means of the lesser rings, and he could see and govern the very thoughts of those that wore them."

Prime Video The One Ring rules the others. There's no doubt about that. In a letter to a publisher in 1951, Tolkien clarified the power of the One Ring over other rings, adding to the description that, along with containing all of the powers of the other Rings, it could see the thoughts and govern their behavior "and in the end could utterly enslave them."

However, the way the One Ring controls the wearers of the "lesser rings" of power isn't consistent. A lot of this depends on who's wearing them. The Elves, for instance, are instantly aware of Sauron when he puts on the One Ring. They're able to understand what's happening and have the willpower to take off their Rings and hide them.

In contrast, the Nine Rings for Mortal Men give Sauron complete control over their owners. "The Silmarillion" says, "They fell under the thraldom of the ring that they bore and under the domination of the One, which was Sauron's." Even when Sauron doesn't have the One Ring, he still has a degree of slavish control over these Men. (What's Elrond's line again? Men are weak.)

That's what Cora (Hunter Schafer) tells Elias (Lewis Gribben) in the penultimate episode of "Blade Runner 2099." The revelation that their adopted mother Helena (Sheila Atim) was actually a replicant — one of the two original Nexus-1 models — shakes Cora to her foundation, and it's the twist through which the show frames its central ideas of what it means to be human. Those questions of passing and authenticity, of whether the differences inherent to replicants are even real, echo even louder through the show's final episode, in which both Cora and Olwen face their humanity in fascinating ways.

Episode 7 ends with Julius (Tom Burke) — the last living Nexus-1 — bombing the replicants' Los Angeles birthing center and making off with the genetic blueprint for his original model. Back at his makeshift lab, he successfully uses the heisted data to extend the life of his partner, Clotilde (Amy Lennox), killing her and rewriting her genetic code to bring her back to life with renewed longevity. Cora and Olwen leave the city in search of them, both desperate to claim the Tyrell memory, and its implications, for themselves.

Throughout its eight episodes, "2099" has shown that its writers understand what "Blade Runner" has always been about: loneliness, empathy, selfishness, love, and the way these forces tangle together to form the inscrutable motivations we identify as human. In its grand finale, "2099" yanks on that knot of emotional strands, leaving some big questions in the best of ways.

In a moment, we'll want to hear what you thought of the final episode. First, let's get into it.

When Hodge tries to turn on them, Olwen shoots him dead, but the pair quickly find more trouble after stumbling into bunk rooms for the newly christened Nexus-1s. In the scuffle, Cora and Olwen both get banged up pretty badly. Clotilde breaks Cora's hand, but since the other replicants are waking up unarmed (and likely disoriented from their recent rebirths), our protagonists manage to kill most of the group.

Cora and Olwen share a brief heart-to-heart after the fight; Cora shares her love for the ocean, and Olwen tries to imagine where she would go after leaving Earth. They then split up to hunt down Julius. Olwen is stalked and ambushed by Clotilde, who seems to have her dead to rights before Olwen begins asking the hard questions: How did it feel to die, and what else is Julius not telling her? Enraged, Clotilde makes a reckless move and trips over a nearby drop-off, nearly falling to her death. At the last second, however, Olwen actually chooses to save her, giving us a glimpse of the empathy that now seems to be rising out of her.

entertainment.title: Duran Duran’s Biggest Billboard Hits: ‘Rio,’ ‘Hungry Like the Wolf’ & More
entertainment.summary: The band sent 15 classics to the Hot 100’s top 40 in the 1980s and ‘90s.
entertainment.body:
Duran Duran charted 15 hits in the top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100 in 1983-93, a run of synth-pop classics, boosted by stylish videos amid MTV’s most tastemaking era, that led to the band ranking among the 100 top-performing acts in the chart’s history.

After John Taylor and Nick Rhodes formed the group in Birmingham, England, in 1978, Duran Duran — by then rounded out by lead singer Simon LeBon, Andy Taylor and Roger Taylor (with none of the Taylors related) — made its Hot 100 debut on Christmas Day 1982 with “Hungry Like the Wolf.” The following March, the single became the group’s first of 11 top 10s, reaching No. 3.

After “Rio” hit No. 14 in May 1983, two more Hot 100 top 10s followed that year: “Is There Something I Should Know” and “Union of the Snake.”

Duran Duran scored its first Hot 100 No. 1, “The Reflex,” in 1984 and added its second, “A View to a Kill,” in 1985, the latter marking the only leader on the list ever from the James Bond film franchise.

Later in the ‘80s, Duran Duran continued to scale the Hot 100’s top 10, while members posted hits via their own ventures, with Andy Taylor joining supergroup Power Station , which scored two top 10s in 1985: “Some Like It Hot” (No. 6) and “Get It On (Bang a Gong)” (No. 9).

Plus, Andy Taylor — who, as announced Nov. 25, died at age 65 — reached No. 24 in 1986 with his solo song “Take It Easy.”

Meanwhile, Arcadia — LeBon, Rhodes and Roger Taylor — notched two top 40 Hot 100 hits in 1985-86, led by the No. 6-peaking “Election Day.”

In 1993, Duran Duran (then comprising LeBon, Rhodes, John Taylor and Warren Cuccurullo), upped its count to 10 and 11 top 10s thanks to “Ordinary World” and “Come Undone.”

entertainment.title: Aaron Rodgers Cut From Steelers After Slamming Coach Mike McCarthy
entertainment.summary: Aaron Rodgers' relationship with his coach entered the red zone. The Pittsburgh Steelers player did not hold back about his opinion of coach Mike McCarthy after learning that he would be punting...
entertainment.body:
Aaron Rodgers ' relationship with his coach entered the red zone.

The Pittsburgh Steelers player did not hold back about his opinion of coach Mike McCarthy after learning that he would be punting the title of starting quarterback. Rodgers lashed out at the NFL coach for surprisingly benching him for the NFL season—in favor of teammate Mason Rudolph —and has since been cut from the team.

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, that word never even came up," Rodgers revealed on Nov. 25 episode of The Pat McAfee Show , referring to "benching." He added that on a phone call with other team leadership he heard, "'I can't believe they're doing this,'" prompting him to ask, "'Doing what?' I didn't know."

And the former Green Bay Packer—who first worked with McCarthy for over a decade in Wisconsin—didn't toe the line when it came to detailing his issues with the 63-year-old, including a claim that McCarthy fell asleep during meetings.

"We were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers, 42, recounted. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers shared that his position stemmed from being "a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy," adding that McCarthy was "not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller."

That said, the Cal alum also stated McCarthy even missed meetings ahead of game day, such as before the Steelers' tough loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22.

And given Rodgers' concerns, he initiated a conversation about changes he believed were mandatory to move forward. In his words, he told McCarthy days before being deemed inactive, "'We got to make a change, like for the betterment of the team.’"

entertainment.title: ‘Twilight’ Director Reveals Robert Pattinson Inspired James Bond Line in 2008 Film: “We Were Seeing the Future”
entertainment.summary: Earlier this month, it was announced that Pattinson has been tapped as the new 007, succeeding Daniel Craig.
entertainment.body:
Catherine Hardwicke , who helmed 2008’s Twilight , might as well have had a crystal ball on the set of the vampire romance film.

After it was revealed earlier this month that Robert Pattinson — who earned his breakout role as Edward Cullen in the blockbuster franchise — had been tapped as the new James Bond , fans were quick to point out that Twilight predicted his 007 casting nearly two decades ago.

At one point in the movie, Eric’s (played by Justin Chon) discusses the prom theme and says, “Gambling, tuxedos, and Bond, James Bond ,” right before the camera cuts to a smirking Edward, looking suave in a pair of sunglasses. Related Stories Movies Prince Harry Approves of Robert Pattinson's Bond Casting Movies The Time Robert Pattinson Snuck Around Rikers Island (and Why It Could Help Him With James Bond)

In a recent interview on The Kyle Buchanan Show , Hardwicke recalled how that line and scene came about. “You guys have probably seen online where we have that [ Twilight ] scene where he [Eric] says, ‘Bond, James Bond,’ and then we cut to Rob,” she said. “That’s the one scene where I was like, ‘Let’s put the sunglasses on that day,’ and he got out of the car and he looked so suave that he inspired the line, ‘Bond, James Bond.’

The director added that Chon “kind of ad-libbed it, and it was kind of cool because we did think he looked like James Bond. So I guess we were seeing the future.”

Fast forward to 2026 and Denis Villeneuve, who’s helming the new 007 movie, and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, obviously thought Pattinson looked like Bond too . The Primetime actor is taking over the iconic role from Daniel Craig, who concluded his run with 2021’s No Time to Die .

Hardwicke also shared her reaction to the news that Pattinson would be going from having “the skin of a killer” to getting his license to kill.

“I almost fell out of my bed,” she quipped about the moment she learned about the casting. “I just didn’t think they were going to choose him because of The Batman and he’s so famous and they like to get the unknown [actor]. So I did almost fall out of the bed, and that is the same bed that Rob and Kristen [Stewart, who played Bella Swan in Twilight ] auditioned for the first time and did their kissing scene. So it was kind of bizarre. And he [Pattinson] fell out of the bed when he did the audition and landed on the floor, so it was kind of cool.”

entertainment.body:
The ongoing legal battle between Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie has finally come to an end.

The Ocean’s Eleven actor and Maleficent star have settled their years-long dispute over the sale of their French winery, Chateau Miraval, which they purchased in 2008 and was the location of their 2014 wedding.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” reps for Jolie and Pitt said in a Nov. 25 statement to E! News. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”

The former couple’s legal woes began in 2022 when Pitt sued Jolie for allegedly selling her interests in their once-shared French estate, according to court documents obtained by E! News at the time.

The Bullet Train actor said in the docs that he had a "mutual and binding commitment" with Jolie that neither one of them would sell their shares to a third party without the other's consent. However, according to the lawsuit, Pitt learned in October 2021 that Tenute del Mondo, a company with ties to Russian billionaire Yuri Shefler , had allegedly bought Jolie's shares of Miraval.

Jolie then filed a $250 million countersuit against Pitt in September of that year, alleging he devised a campaign to "seize control" of the once-shared estate after their 2016 split. This lawsuit, obtained by E! News at the time, alleged that Jolie only sold her portion of the estate to an outside company when Pitt refused to remove the NDA stipulations he'd included as part of the deal.

The legal saga got even more intense when Jolie accused Pitt of abuse in a cross complaint obtained by E! News in October 2022 . In the court docs, Jolie addressed a 2016 airplane incident that allegedly occurred days before she decided to file for divorce , in which she alleged that Pitt had choked one of their children.

More allegations came out in April 2024 when Jolie filed documents stating, “While Pitt's history of physical abuse of Jolie started well before the family's September 2016 plane trip from France to Los Angeles, this flight marked the first time he turned his physical abuse on the children as well. Jolie then immediately left him."

The new album was preceded by its lead single “Silencio,” which marked the group’s 45th entry on the Alternative Airplay chart earlier in November (tying Foo Fighters for the most in the chart’s history). On Wednesday night (Nov. 25), U2 will headline the halftime show of the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, which kicks off at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. entertainment.summary: If your Turkey Day plans include watching the parade, be prepared for some deflating news. The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in history, with the...
entertainment.body:
If your Turkey Day plans include watching the parade, be prepared for some deflating news.

The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in history, with the milestone 100th celebration being delayed two days until Nov. 28 due to a severe storm headed to New York City, an NBC spokesperson confirmed to E! News.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided,” the spokesperson shared in a Nov. 25 statement, “in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28. More details to follow.”

Macy’s expressed gratitude for the many people who bring the parade to living rooms every Thanksgiving.

“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year,” a spokesperson told MSNOW in a statement. “We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

And while the announcement marks the first time the parade has been postponed since its debut in 1924, the Thanksgiving Day staple has been cancelled three times throughout its 100-year history—from 1942 to 1944—due to World War II.

This year, the monumental centennial celebration was set to take place on Thursday, when a coastal storm is predicted the Big Apple and eastern coastline, bringing rain and strong winds.

This poses a major safety concern not only for the millions of New Yorkers who watch the parade in person, but also for the thousands of performers who participate, alongside the nearly 30 floats and record-breaking 100 inflatables , which will include characters such as Bluey, Buckaroo Bob the Minion and Hello Kitty.

entertainment.title: ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Producer Alex Gayner Thought He’d Solved Every Problem a Set Could Throw at Him. Then Came a Runaway Parrot.
entertainment.summary: Ten seconds of footage ended up being the most nerve-wracking part of the shoot for the movie veteran who has been on sets since the '90s.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Filmmakers often thrive on controlled chaos. Alex Gayner has spent his career orchestrating that madness.

Long before producing The Mosquito Bowl for Peter Berg , Gayner cut his teeth doing odd jobs on ’90s direct-to-video actioners — the kind of movies you’d stumble across on a pay-cable channel at 1 AM during a bout of insomnia. Then, a second assistant director was let go before lunch, and Gayner found himself promoted on the spot. It was an unlikely break that set the course for the rest of his career.

He gradually climbed the ranks to first assistant director, eventually trading B-movies for some of the biggest studio productions around, including Guillermo del Toro’s Pacific Rim and Gareth Edwards’ Godzilla . He also developed a reputation as a closer, overseeing reshoots for Suicide Squad (2016), Birds of Prey , Zero Dark Thirty and Mulan , among others. Related Stories TV 'Beef' Creator Lee Sung Jin Launches Production Company, Plans Ali Wong Limited Series Movies Ray Nicholson Levels Up With 'The Mosquito Bowl': "I'm Always Battling for Legitimacy"

Another turning point arrived in the late 2010s, when the native New Yorker decided to pivot to producing. If the first AD is the on-set quarterback who executes the plays on the field, then Gayner wanted to become a full-time offensive coordinator, the person drawing up the plays and mapping out the production behind the scenes.

He credits Nicolas Winding Refn with giving him his big break as a producer on the 2019 limited series Too Old to Die Young , an opportunity that paved the way for him to produce the first season of Beef and win an Emmy for his work. (Gayner and Refn are now assembling the latter’s long-gestating Maniac Cop reimagining, which recently received approval for a California tax credit.)

After wrapping Beef , Netflix pointed Gayner toward Berg’s 19th-century Western limited series American Primeval . But first, the two had to bridge the gap between the producer Berg expected and the one Gayner turned out to be.

“When I met Pete, I don’t think he really knew what kind of producer I was,” Gayner tells The Hollywood Reporter . “Naturally, he didn’t know if I was going to come in to watch the money or try to make the show on soundstages. We had to figure each other out.”

To keep the football metaphors going, Berg likes to run his sets with a no-huddle offense, frequently calling audibles along the way. He might improvise dialogue, change camera positions or throw out the playbook altogether. Most of all, he has a strict devotion to immersive, practical filmmaking. Fortunately, Gayner has been adapting on the fly ever since that lunchtime promotion more than 30 years ago. He also shares Berg’s preference for capturing as much as possible in camera.

The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday, shortly after he torched Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show .

The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday’s visit from Denver. Rodgers told McAfee he found out about the surprise decision while on the phone with teammates, including tight end Pat Freiermuth.

It was just the start of a blistering offensive from Rodgers, who painted McCarthy — whom he played under during a long successful run in Green Bay earlier in their careers — as a leader woefully out of touch.

He described a quarterback meeting last Wednesday with McCarthy arriving late, sat down “and within 10 minutes began snoring,” woke up and nodded off again minutes later, then eventually “walks out of the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers also said McCarthy missed an offensive meeting Thursday, missed a walkthrough Friday and a morning meeting Saturday while not holding a team meeting that night.

“And then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled and the product wasn’t great,” Rodgers said, adding that McCarthy broke up the halftime locker room meeting by saying “1-2-3 Packers.”

Rodgers said he felt it was the right thing to bring up the issues to McCarthy as a longtime league star instead of putting it on others with fewer years, shaky roster positions or those who “haven’t made $400 million dollars in the NFL.”

entertainment.title: King Crimson Co-Founder Michael Giles Dead at 84
entertainment.summary: As part of Giles, Giles, and Fripp, he'd laid the sound that would change prog rock forever when he helpd form King Crimson to record In the Court of the Crimson King
entertainment.body:
Michael Giles, a drummer and singer who cofounded King Crimson , died Monday, according to King Crimson’s record label, DGM , which did not report a cause of death. Giles was 84.

“Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world,” Crimson’s label said. “He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”

Giles’ musical beginnings with Giles, Giles, and Fripp, a trio he cofounded in 1967 in Bournemouth — where was he was born on March 1, 1942 — with his brother Peter and guitarist Robert Fripp, were inauspicious, at least by King Crimson standards. The band’s only album, 1968’s The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp , was all psychedelia: shimmering organ, pensive vocals, and relatively straightforward, march-like drumming that only occasionally hinted at jazziness. It’s straightforward pop rock, but you can also hear how it provided the framework for King Crimson’s outré, ponderous adventures a year later.

When Peter quit to become a solicitor’s clerk in November 1968, Michael and Fripp wanted to continue making music, so they formed King Crimson with Greg Lake, who’d played bass with the Gods, and multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald. The lineup included Peter Sinfield as lyricist and lighting director. Together, the conceived an album that would define the sound of prog rock in the early Seventies: In the Court of the Crimson King , which came out in 1969.

The album’s seven-minute opening cut, “21st Century Schizoid Man,” was an FM radio hit in spite of its turn-on-a-dime rhythm changes and extended bass and sax duets. The stylistic shift allowed Giles to challenge himself to make his drum parts more musical, whether mirroring McDonald’s sax or rolling rhythms like waves in the main riff. “The Court of the Crimson King,” a 10-minute musical journey, took the streamlined rock sound of Giles, Giles, and Fripp and augmented it with flute, Mellotron, and choral-like harmonies. Giles’ drumming on the song is the musical equivalent to expressionism as he brings out his bandmates’ drama. He latter cited Elvin Jones, who’d played with John Coltrane, as an inspiration. The Hawk , co-created by Ferrell and Harper Steele, followed disgraced pro golfer Lonnie Hawkins (Ferrell) who seeks to regain his former glory. entertainment.title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65
entertainment.summary: He served as the band's guitarist during their commercial height and later became a founding member of the supergroup The Power Station.
entertainment.body:
Andy Taylor, Duran Duran ‘s guitarist during the band’s commercial peak in the 1980s as well as a founding member of supergroup The Power Station, has died. He was 65

Taylor died following a battle with prostate cancer, his family and Duran Duran announced Wednesday on social media.

“To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather,” his wife, Tracey Taylor, said in a statement. “He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.” Related Stories Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87 TV Steven Hack, Original 'Cats' Castmember and Busy Onscreen Character Actor, Dies at 68

As the band said in a statement of its own: “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

The Englishman wasn’t technically a founding member of Duran Duran, but he joined the group in 1980 before they recorded their eponymous 1981 debut album, and he served as the guitarist through the band’s commercial zenith on their next two albums Rio and Seven and the Ragged Tiger .

He left amid the recording of the group’s fourth album, Notorious , but rejoined Duran Duran from 2001 to 2006 and appeared on the band’s 2023 album, Danse Macabre , as well.

Taylor co-wrote several of the band’s biggest hits, including “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “Rio” and “Girls on Film.”

He entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame with the group in 2022. His battle with cancer prevented him from attending the induction ceremony, with the group reading a letter Taylor wrote instead.

entertainment.body:
Paramount Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine" showrunner Ira Steven Behr struggles with the iconic episode "Trials and Tribble-ations" for the exact reason that so many Trekkies love it and consider it one of the must-watch "Deep Space Nine" episodes .

"Trials and Tribble-ations" aired in the 5th season of "Deep Space Nine," the '90s "Star Trek" series named for a wormhole-adjacent space station that hosts the adventures of its motley crew. The fan-favorite episode sees the inhabitants of Deep Space Nine transported back in time to the era of the "Star Trek" original series. "Star Trek" fans immediately rejoiced upon seeing the DS9 crew inevitably join forces with the crew of the USS Enterprise — and while Ira Steven Behr felt pleased with the episode's positive reception, he also chafed against its nostalgic tone.

"The only thing that bugs me about ["Trials and Tribble-ations"] is that it feeds off the myth of the franchise," Behr revealed in the 2000 reference book "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine Companion." The episode was indeed written as a tribute for the original series' 30th anniversary. It replicated the early "Star Trek" franchise's style by digitally editing the "DS9" actors into footage from the original series' beloved "Star Trek" episode "The Trouble with Tribbles." Behr continued, "The fact that it's so popular saddens me in a way, in the sense that I wish a show that is 'Deep Space Nine' intensive didn't have to lean on the history."

Paramount/YouTube During the annual Trek Talks telethon in March 2026, Ira Steven Behr said many of the "DS9" team members felt "lukewarm" about making a "Star Trek" homage episode from the get-go, but a "once-in-a-lifetime" coincidence convinced them of the episode's near-cosmic importance. Shortly after the "Deep Space Nine" team had settled on the original series episode that they wanted to honor, they began discussing potential actors from "The Trouble with Tribbles" they could find to appear in "Trials and Tribble-ations" over lunch at an LA pizzeria.

"I said, 'The only person I know who's definitely alive from the guest cast was this guy named Charlie Brill' ... who played Arne Darvin, the Klingon who was now undercover as a human being," Behr shared. He continued, "Then I look over, and standing at the counter ordering a slice of pizza ... is freaking Charlie Brill."

entertainment.title: Andy Taylor, Former Duran Duran Guitarist, Dead at 65
entertainment.summary: The rocker had been battling prostate cancer for about eight years.
entertainment.body:
Andy Taylor , guitarist and former member of Duran Duran , has died after a yearslong battle with prostate cancer. He was 65 years old.

The musician’s former bandmates shared the news Wednesday (Nov. 25) on their website and on Instagram , announcing that Taylor had passed away two days prior. “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story,” the group wrote. “From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.”

Duran Duran continued, “His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

Still in its early years, the band added Taylor to the lineup in 1980. He would leave in 1986 before rejoining in 2001, playing guitar on Duran Duran’s 2004 album Astronaut (which reached No. 17 on the Billboard 200 ) before leaving again in 2006. In 2023, he’d contribute guitar to Halloween-themed LP Danse Macabre .

During his time in the group, Duran Duran scored 13 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 , including two No. 1s: “The Reflex” in 1984 and “A View to a Kill” in 1985. The group’s blockbuster Rio album (which housed “Hungry Like the Wolf”) hit the Billboard 200 in 1982 and remained on the chart a staggering 128 weeks. As a soloist, he scored two entries on the chart: “Take It Easy” (No. 24 in 1986) and “When the Rain Comes Down” (No. 73 in 1986). As a member of the supergroup The Power Station, he earned three top 40 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985.

Taylor’s wife, Tracey, also shared a statement Wednesday. “To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather,” she wrote. “He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first.”

His cancer diagnosis was first revealed in 2022, when frontman Simon LeBon told fans at Duran Duran’s induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame — which Taylor did not attend, though he was inducted alongside his bandmates — that he’d already been battling the illness for four years at that point. In 2023, Taylor shared that he’d started taking cancer drug Lutetium-177, which he said extended his life by five years.

entertainment.title: Hold Your Turkeys! Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade Has Been Postponed: Here’s the New Date
entertainment.summary: As it turns out, Mother Nature spares no man nor parade.
entertainment.body:
After waiting 100 years for the parade’s centennial edition, what’s a few more days?

Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day parade will be postponed to Saturday, Nov. 28, because of severe weather.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s representatives said Wednesday.

Even though organizers had already begun inflating the parade’s iconic balloons, the department store, alongside city officials and the New York Police Department, confirmed the Thanksgiving celebration will commence n Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET instead.

The parade’s delay comes amid a particularly grim forecast for the East Coast. The National Weather Service is predicting a strong storm will impact the area on Thanksgiving Day, inundating it with heavy rain, intense winds and coastal flooding.

RAYE, who recently earned a record-tying 11 nominations at the 2027 Grammys, is set to open the broadcast, which will air on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo. The historic parade will march from the Upper West Side to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store, and include performances by Billboard chart-topping stars Megan Mooney and Teddy Swims. Tony and Grammy-nominated Broadway star Megan Hilty will lead a tribute to the late Dolly Parton, who passed in August at age 80.

Other celebrities to keep an eye out for in the parade’s eye-popping floats include EJAE of KPop Demon Hunters girl group HUNTR/X, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, JoJo, Keke Palmer, Smash Mouth, Mckenna Grace, K-pop boy band RIIZE, Indigo Girls, Natasha Bedingfield, Feid, Icona Pop, Wyclef Jean, Jamie Miller, Leslie Odom Jr., Anthony Ramos, Melissa Joan Hart, Jamie Miller, Holly Robinson Peete and more.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade first marched New York City’s streets in 1924, and it’s only been canceled three times: 1942, 1943 and 1944. During those years, materials for giant balloons were prioritized for World War II efforts over holiday parades. Notably, the balloons were last grounded in 1971 due to severe weather; city regulations dictate that balloons can only fly when wind speeds remain below 23 mph. In 2019, inclement weather forced the balloons to be flown at lower heights than usual.

entertainment.title: With ‘Guarding Stars,’ Jared Padalecki Finally Takes A Break From All That Action
entertainment.summary: The 'Walker' and 'Supernatural' star enjoys a change of pace in Netflix's latest romantic comedy, based on Katherine Center's 'The Bodyguard.'
entertainment.body:
Jared Padalecki has been steadily employed on television since his days on aughts classic Gilmore Girls , so it’d be easy to assume that playing an actor in the new Netflix holiday offering Guarding Stars would be second nature. But the 44-year-old, who also produces the movie, found the role to be more difficult than he’d expected.

“Jack Stapleton in this world is super famous,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter about this character. “He’s Brad Pitt, he’s George Clooney, he’s Chris Hemsworth — people who can’t walk outside. After 26 years in the industry, I can walk outside.” Related Stories Beyond the Book From Book Club to Netflix: How Katherine Center's 'The Bodyguard' Became 'Guarding Stars' Movies 'Guarding Stars' Trailer: Leighton Meester, Jared Padalecki Star in Fake-Dating Holiday Romance

It’s not as though Padalecki is claiming to fly completely under-the-radar. He admits that he’ll often encounter people in public who stop him to share their love for Supernatural or Gilmore Girls , but he’s still able to go to his son’s games or his daughter’s field hockey practices. It helps, certainly, that he and his wife, actress and fellow Guarding Stars producer Genevieve Padalecki, live in a ranch outside Austin, Texas, rather than in Los Angeles.

Guarding Stars , released on the streamer on Nov. 18, is based on Katherine Center’s romance novel The Bodyguard and features a delightful role reversal. Rather than Padalecki, who’s spent much of his adult life starring in action-driven projects, as the dutiful protector, his character Jack finds himself under the care of bodyguard Hannah Brooks, played by Leighton Meester.

The book, while not set at Christmas, has the same spirit as its onscreen adaptation. The Padaleckis were responsible for getting the project off the ground after Gen Padalecki featured Center’s book in her online book club and interviewed the author four years ago.

When the interview ended, Gen Padalecki told Center that she thought the book would make a great movie. The author agreed, and the couple soon had acquired the rights and began shopping the project around. Eventually, it landed at Netflix, underwent a name change and found its badass leading lady in Meester and formable leading man in Padalecki. Center, throughout it all, took any changes to her material in stride, Padalecki says, mimicking her response when changes would arise, “It’s not a documentary.”

Clinching the Mirrorball trophy was music to Ezra Frech ’s ears.

Especially since the Paralympian had to power through an ear injury while taking to the dance floor on the season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars Nov. 24.

The 21-year-old raised eyebrows when fans spotted blood on his face after his freestyle performance with partner Daniella Karagach—but it turns out he’d gotten scratched from one of her costumes earlier in the show.

“I’m so freaking sorry,” Karagach exclaimed to Frech in her Nov. 24 Instagram Story. “Are you OK though?”

Frech assured her that he was indeed “fine,” joking that the cuts along his face and his ear were just “battle scars.”

Still, the dance pro was mortified by what her costume had done, exclaiming, “Oh my gosh, your ear. Dude. My dress.”

The track and field star acknowledged that the injury was quite noticeable , adding, “People were like, ‘Your ear was bleeding when you were getting interviewed.’”

Karagach gave her partner one final apology before the duo took to the ballroom for the live finale , waltzing into the history books as Frech became the first amputee and the youngest man to win Dancing With the Stars .

sports.title: Rams move ahead 20-13 on Blake Corum TD
sports.summary: The Rams took more than eight minutes off the clock before taking the lead.
sports.body:
Corum ran nine time for 35 yards during a 15-play Rams drive and the final yard he picked up was a touchdown that broke a tie and put the Rams up 13-10. The drive opened the third quarter and ate up eight minutes of playing time.

The Rams faced three third downs on the drive and had Matthew Stafford throw to wide receiver Konata Mumpfield each time. The first two were completions that picked up 30 yards and the third was initially ruled a touchdown on the field. Replays showed Mumpfield did not have control of the ball in the end zone, but the Rams still got a first down due to a defensive holding penalty on the day.

Corum has 16 carries for 58 yards and Mumpfield has four catches for 69 yards.

sports.title: Christian Watson ruled out with a concussion
sports.summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was disqualified for the hit that injured Watson.
sports.body:
Watson went to the locker room for a concussion evaluation shortly before halftime and the Packers announced that he has been ruled out at the start of the second half. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to his injury.

The Rams also lost safety Kamren Kinchens for the rest of the game on the same play. Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson.

Rams tight end Davis Allen has also been ruled out with an ankle injury.

The two teams went to the break tied 13-13 and that remains the score early in the third quarter.

sports.title: Here's a roadmap to the Aaron Rodgers developments, one of the craziest stories in years
sports.summary: If you were traveling on Wednesday or otherwise not plugged in for one of the most rollicking, unpredictable days in years if not ever, you're in luck.
sports.body:
We’ve reconstructed the full timeline as to the events regarding now-former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

It actually started on Monday, when coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether he has considered using one of the team’s other three quarterbacks when the offense is struggling. McCarthy, whose body language in hindsight suggests he was dreading the question , said without equivocation, “ Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback .”

On Tuesday, Rodgers took his usual reps at practice. He conducted his usual midweek press conference. Unbeknownst to most of the media or the general public, the Steelers were changing their play-calling procedures to have quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, and not McCarthy, communicate the calls to Rodgers through the speaker in his helmet.

Then came Tuesday night. At 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers issued a statement — not from coach Mike McCarthy or G.M. Omar Khan or owner Art Rooney II but from team spokesman Burt Lauten — that Mason Rudolph will start on Friday against the Broncos and Rodgers will be inactive.

The news forced the Broncos to make a quick pivot in their preparations from Rodgers to Rudolph. As one source put it, the Broncos weren’t sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing .

It was definitely a bad thing, all things considered, for the Steelers.

By Wednesday morning, reports emerged that it was a coach’s decision . At 8:00 a.m. ET, McCarthy informed the team of the decision.

Enter Pat McAfee. He teased a surprise guest at 1:40 p.m. ET. As expected, it was Rodgers.

sports.title: Micah Parsons gets first sack of season, Packers and Rams tied 13-13 at halftime
sports.summary: Parsons's sack came just before end of the first half in Los Angeles.
sports.body:
Parsons made his return from a torn ACL against the Rams and had a couple of pressures early in the game. He got home for a sack of Matthew Stafford on the Rams’ first play after a Trey Smack field goal tied the score at 13-13 with 1:50 to play in the half.

The Rams ran out the clock from there and they will get the ball to start the second half at SoFi Stadium.

Parsons’s sack was part of an eventful final couple of minutes. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a hit to the head of Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and Watson is now being evaluated for a concussion. It would be a big loss for the Packers as Watson has four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown so far on Wednesday night.

Running back Kyren Williams scored the Rams’ only touchdown, but their offense slowed down after picking up points on each of their first three possessions. Stafford is 12-of-15 for 98 yards while Williams and Blake Corum have 35 yards on nine carries.

Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 12-of-18 for 154 yards. The Packers will be hoping for right guard Kevin Zeitler’s return from an ankle injury while waiting for more word on Watson and the Rams called tight end Davis Allen to return from an ankle injury.

sports.title: Rams S Kamren Kinchens ejected for hit on Christian Watson
sports.summary: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after a hit on wide receiver Christian Watson.
sports.body:
Per the Netflix broadcast, the league office said that Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and making helmet-to-helmet contact with Watson and NFL executive vice president Troy Vincent made the final call on disqualifying him from the game.

Watson held onto the ball, but went to the locker room with members of the medical staff and the catch did not count because Packers wideout Matthew Golden was flagged for offensive pass interference to offset the Kinchens foul.

The play came on a fourth-and-1 and the Packers ultimately opted to kick a field goal rather than go for it again. It is now 13-13 with under two minutes to play in the half.

sports.title: Jordan Love, Christian Watson cut Rams lead to 13-10
sports.summary: The points keep coming in the first half at SoFi Stadium.
sports.body:
A little more than three minutes after the Rams scored their first touchdown of the night, the Packers paid their first visit to the end zone. Jordan Love hooked up with Christian Watson for a six-yard score that cut the Rams’ lead to 13-10 with just over eight minutes to play in the half.

Watson also caught a pass on the first play of the drive and that completion went for 21 yards. Love hit Watson’s fellow wideout Matthew Golden for a 39-yard gain on the next play and the quarterback scrambled for the third first down of the possession a couple of plays after that big gain.

The Packers went three-and-out and turned the ball over on their first two possessions, but they are now outgaining the Rams thanks to back-to-back scoring drives.

sports.title: Kyren Williams makes it 13-3 Rams in second quarter
sports.summary: The Rams have had the ball three times and all three drives have ended in points.
sports.body:
Running back Kyren Williams finished off the third possession with a seven-yard sprint into the end zone that pushed the Rams’ lead over the Packers to 13-3 with 11:29 to play in the first half. It’s the first time the Rams have scored on their first three possessions this season and it’s also the first time the Packers have allowed their opponents points on their first three drives.

Most of the other movement on the drive came through the air. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed passes to Williams, tight end Davis Allen, wide receiver Konata Mumpfield, and tight end Tyler Higbee for first downs before Williams’s touchdown. The throw to Williams came just before Stafford took a hit from Packers defensive end Micah Parsons.

Stafford is 10-of-12 for 87 yards while Jordan Love is 6-of-10 for 70 yards, including a 32-yarder to Christian Watson that set up Trey Smack’s 54-yard field goal.

sports.title: Rams extend lead to 6-0 after Tucker Kraft fumble
sports.summary: The Rams doubled their lead after forcing the first turnover of Wednesday night's game.
sports.body:
Linebacker Nate Landman punched the ball out of tight end Tucker Kraft’s hands and safety Quentin Lake recovered the ball on the Rams’ 43-yard-line. The play came one snap after a Kam Curl interception was wiped out by an illegal contact penalty.

The Rams picked up a first down when Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt was flagged for roughing Matthew Stafford and added another on a 15-yard pass to Konata Mumpfield. Packers defensive end Micah Parsons pressured Stafford into an incompletion on the next play and a botched backward pass cost the Rams six yards before they settled for Brandon McManus’s second field goal.

sports.title: Rams lead 3-0, Christian Watson makes quick return from thigh injury
sports.summary: The Rams are out to an early lead at SoFi Stadium.
sports.body:
After forcing a quick Packers punt, the Rams ran three times for a first down. Matthew Stafford’s first pass of the game was a deep shot to wide receiver Xavier Smith that fell incomplete, but Packers rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was flagged for pass interference.

The play picked up 37 yards for the home team, but three straight completions by Stafford only picked up seven more yards and Brandon McManus was called on for a field goal that made it 3-0 with 9:55 to play in the first quarter.

The Packers opened the game with a six-yard pass to wide receiver Christian Watson, but he needed medical attention after the play. The team called him questionable to return with a thigh injury, but he was back on the field after the Rams kicked the ball off.

In the early decades of the NFL preceding the 1940s — back when lights on funny looking cars, street lamps, and those indoors were still sometimes powered by oil and kerosene, and a short while later by carbide gas — Wednesday games were not unusual. Since 1940? Before tonight, six NFL games of notoriety were played on a Wednesday in the last 86 years, and none from 1949 through 2011. This evening, the Los Angeles Rams, Green Bay Packers, and the NFL get a new “holiday” all to themselves. sports.title: Steelers should have known Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy couldn't co-exist
sports.summary: Someone in the organization should have said a reunion cannot happen.
sports.body:
The reporting of Tyler Dunne, who at the time wrote for Bleacher Report , made it clear that there were issues between them during the latter years of McCarthy’s time with the Packers. Rodgers took it to another level on Wednesday, telling Pat McAfee and company that McCarthy believed Rodgers got him fired by the Packers — and that McCarthy had done some of the things he’s been doing with the Steelers when McCarthy coached the Packers.

If McCarthy believes Rodgers got him fired by the Packers, why in the world would McCarthy want Rodgers in his Pittsburgh locker room? It’s ludicrous. It’s asinine. It’s self-destructive.

From Rodgers’s perspective, why in the world would he want to play for McCarthy again? Although Rodgers said Wednesday that he believed McCarthy would be different given it’s Rodgers’s last year in the NFL and McCarthy’s first year in his dream job, it was naive for Rodgers to think that, at 63, McCarthy would suddenly start working harder than he ever has.

Oh, they tried to sell us on the idea that he would. “ Attention to detail ” became a talking point during training camp. Plenty of media members swallowed the hook.

Rodgers knew better. But he ignored his own experiences with McCarthy — in the same way McCarthy ignored his own experiences with Rodgers.

The situation cried out for someone, anyone in the organization to stand up and say, “Are we nuts? Once adversity strikes, this situation will crumble. And it will take us with it.”

It didn’t just crumble. It imploded into one of the most embarrassing situations any NFL franchise has endured in years, if not ever.

As the saying goes, when you dance with the devil, you don’t change the devil. The devil changes you. By allowing McCarthy and Rodgers to reprise their Lambeau rumba, the Steelers thought the music would stop in the postseason. Instead, McCarthy and Rodgers have pulled a franchise with six Super Bowl trophies into the eighth circle of dysfunction.

sports.title: Report: G.M. Omar Khan called Aaron Rodgers directly to inform him of the benching
sports.summary: As expected, the Steelers view the events that resulted in the benching and eventual release of quarterback Aaron Rodgers differently than Rodgers does.
sports.body:
On one very specific point — as it relates to whether the Steelers properly handled the situation — the Steelers and Rodgers sharply disagree.

Rodgers said Wednesday that he learned he’d be benched and inactive when tight end Pat Freiermuth called Rodgers, after the announcement of the move was made at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday night. However, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported during the Wednesday night pregame show that G.M. Omar Khan called Rodgers to inform him of the change to Mason Rudolph.

It’s odd, to say the least, that the Steelers announced the move after 11:00 p.m. local time on a Tuesday night. If Rodgers didn’t know, there was no reason to let the world (and specifically the Broncos) know the move had been made.

The mere fact that the Steelers announced it when they did suggests that Rodgers knew about the decision, and that the Steelers believed he possibly would release it in terms that supported his broader version of the events.

By announcing it on Tuesday night, the Steelers pre-empted a late-night social-media post from Rodgers — or a strategic leak to a reporter — painting the situation in the light most favorable to Rodgers. For example, Rodgers could have characterized that he was benched because he was repeatedly blowing the whistle internally about coach Mike McCarthy’s various alleged lapses.

While it’s a minor point, it points to the broader issue of credibility. If Rodgers knew about the decision, any suggestion that he didn’t would be calculated to make the Steelers look inept for telling the world he’d been benched without letting him know about it in advance.

The truth may never be fully known. But it’s clear that, as to the things that happened over the past day or two, there are (as there always seems to be) two versions — Rodgers’s version and the team’s version.

It’s also possible there are three versions. Rodgers’s version, the Steelers’ version, and the truth.

sports.body:
“There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him,” McCarthy said.

Asked to explain what he meant by that, McCarthy wouldn’t directly answer.

“I’m not going to get into all those specifics. I know you have to ask the question, but those conversations are better served — they’re private conversations,” McCarthy told reporters.

McCarthy said he and every player should take pride in being a Pittsburgh Steeler, and conduct himself like a Steeler.

“We’re all fortunate to work here. This is an incredible opportunity, to work for the Pittsburgh Steelers,” McCarthy said.

The most direct answer McCarthy gave to a question today was when a reporter asked if Rodgers had been released. McCarthy simply answered, “Yes.”

sports.summary: The Steelers are planning no "immediate" changes.
sports.body:
Via ESPNFL, McCarthy “ has the full support of the organization ,” and "[t]hey are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes.”

The use of the term “immediate” is curious. Is this just a matter of getting through the season before taking a closer look at the situation?

Regardless, Rodgers dropped a fairly sizable turd into the confluence of the Ohio, Allegheny, and Monongahela Rivers. If his claims about McCarthy are true, McCarthy is objectively unfit to coach the team.

At this point, there’s not much that can be done. They play a game on Friday afternoon. Besides, they’re 6-4 and fighting for a spot in the playoffs.

While the situation is far from ideal, the Steelers are opting to stay the course for now. Likely because it’s too late to change direction.

The real question is whether, after the season, McCarthy will be given a chance to step down. And, if not, whether he’ll be fired.

Barring a postseason berth and the first playoff win since the 2016 season, it’s hard to envision the situation being sustainable. Which could result in a team that had three coaches from 1969 through 2025 having two in two years.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy confirms he said "1-2-3 Packers" at halftime last Sunday
sports.summary: Aaron Rodgers said a number of things that caught the attention of the football world on Wednesday and one of the comments that drew a big response had to do with something that happened in the locker room at halftime of last Sunday's loss to the Eagles.
sports.body:
After saying head coach Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meetings and missed other ones altogether in his first comments since being benched on Tuesday night, Rodgers said that McCarthy broke down the team in the locker room with “1-2-3 Packers” in reference to the team he coached through the 2018 season. In a press conference later in the day, McCarthy confirmed that happened but said he took issue with how Rodgers characterized other things that included his commitment to the job.

“The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional. . . . Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments,” McCarthy said.

The Steelers have released Rodgers and McCarthy stressed the need for the team to focus on Friday’s game against the Broncos, although it feels like that’s going to be difficult based on how the last 18 hours have played out in Pittsburgh.

The NFL’s daily transaction report shows that Rodgers has been released on Wednesday afternoon. That was the expected move from the team after Rodgers’s incendiary comments about head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show earlier in the day.

Rodgers was responding to the team’s decision to bench him ahead of Friday’s game against the Broncos. News of that move came late on Tuesday night, which was one day after McCarthy said Rodgers would remain the starter.

Rodgers will be available on waivers and will become a free agent if the league’s other 31 teams pass on the chance on adding him to their roster for the final weeks of what Rodgers has said will be his final NFL season.

sports.title: Steelers could try to not pay Aaron Rodgers the balance of his $22 million salary
sports.summary: If/when the Steelers release quarterback Aaron Rodgers, they'll have to decide whether to willingly pay the balance of his $22 million base salary, or whether to fight.
sports.body:
With his Week 12 paycheck already vested, the question becomes Week 13 through Week 18. Six weeks, totaling $7.33 million.

It won’t be easy to cut him off. First, the Steelers would have to release him for reasons unrelated to skill, injury, or salary cap. The argument, if the Steelers make it, would be that Rodgers’s appearance on Pat McAfee’s show constitutes personal conduct detrimental to the interests of the team .

A grievance would undoubtedly be filed, if the Steelers pursue that approach.

But even without the guarantee, Rodgers’s presence on the Week 1 roster qualifies him for the balance of his base salary as “termination pay” under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. To circumvent that, the Steelers would have to show that Rodgers has become ineligible for termination pay.

Here’s the key language, from Article 30, Section 3(b) of the CBA: “An otherwise qualified player will not be entitled to Termination Pay if (i) the Club terminated the player’s contract for Conduct Detrimental to the Club, and (ii) the Non-Injury Grievance Arbitrator determines that the player’s conduct was so severe that the maximum discipline for Conduct Detrimental of a fine equal to one week’s salary and suspension without pay for four weeks, pursuant to Article 42, Section 1(b)(xvii) of this Agreement (regardless of whether the Club imposed any such discipline prior to terminating the player’s contract), constitutes an inadequate remedy for the player’s conduct.”

It won’t be easy to satisfy that standard. But there’s language in the CBA that potentially applies to Rodgers’s public comments from Wednesday.

Here’s Article 6, titled “Public Statements": “The NFLPA and the Management Council agree that each will use reasonable efforts to curtail public comments by Club personnel or players which express criticism of any club, its coach, or its operation and policy, or which tend to cast discredit upon a Club, a player, or any other person involved in the operation of a Club, the NFL, the Management Council, or the NFLPA.”

That’s the same clause that fueled the NFL’s attack against the NFL Players Association’s report cards. The process constitutes comments from the NFLPA that express criticism of the teams, their coaches, the operations, and their policies.

sports.title: Pat Freiermuth: Aaron Rodgers said what he said, I'm focused on Denver
sports.summary: While Aaron Rodgers was going scorched earth on the Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy during Wednesday's appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, he said that tight end Pat Freiermuth informed him of the team's decision to bench him on Tuesday night.
sports.body:
Rodgers was on the show while the Steelers were practicing, but Freiermuth spoke to reporters in the team’s locker room later in the day. He said he “was just checking in on a close friend” when he called Rodgers after hearing the news of the quarterback change and said he otherwise had nothing to add to what Rodgers said earlier in the day.

“Anything I say about the situation is gonna be tough and obviously it’s tough ,” Freiermuth said, via Mark Kaboly of the McAfee show. “I’m here and we’re just focused on trying to get a win against Denver. Obviously he said what he said, but I’m focused on the locker room and the team. That’s really all I have to say about that.”

Rodgers said that others on the roster share his dismay with the way McCarthy has handled his job responsibilities this year and Freiermuth was asked if he has confidence in the team’s direction. Freiermuth said “I’m confident” before declining other requests to comment on topics that came up during a Rodgers appearance that’s likely to remain a talking point around the team for some time.

sports.title: Joe Brady can become the fifth coach ever to win 10 of his first 11 games
sports.summary: Buffalo's Joe Brady is off to one of the best starts for any head coach in NFL history.
sports.body:
The Bills are 9-1, which means that if they beat the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Brady will be just the fifth coach in NFL history to win 10 of his first 11 games.

The four who have done it before are Jim Caldwell (11-0 with the 2009 Colts), Wally Lemm (who went 9-0 as interim head coach of the 1961 Houston Oilers and then won one of his first two games after becoming head coach of the 1962 St. Louis Cardinals), Steve Mariucci (10-1 with the 1997 49ers) and Red Miller (10-1 with the 1977 Broncos).

Brady took over a good Bills team and has kept them near the top of the NFL. His record to start his head-coaching career is impressive, but he was brought in to win in the postseason, and so it’s too soon to say whether the Bills’ decision to fire Sean McDermott and replace him with Brady will pay off.

Dorian Williams and Christian Benford, on the other hand, are more likely to be game day decisions. Soft tissue injuries aren’t fun. sports.body: What do I think is the biggest — and most specific — defensive key for the Buffalo Bills against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night? I’ll provide some metrics, and you’ll be able to reach the answer. The Chiefs are: * First in screen-pass rate in the NFL entering this game at 16.4% * Third in RPO rate at 8.4% and Patrick Mahomes has the: * Third-lowest average depth of target (aDOT) at 6.6 yards among 38 qualifiers * Fourth-quickest average time to attempt at 2.51 seconds among those same qualifiers * Fourth-lowest percentage of throws made 20-plus yards downfield at 9.2% among 33 qualifiers * Second-highest adjusted completion percentage at 81.1% You guessed it — tackling. The Chiefs, more than any other offense, put their opponents’ tackling capabilities to the test. How well have the Bills tackled this season, you ask? Below is a graphic that demonstrates the total amount of missed tackles credited to Bills defenders in each game by Pro Football Focus to date this season: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/correct-bills-missed-tckles-thru-wk11-1.png?quality=90&strip=all] After the bye week, which coincides with when CJ Gardner-Johnson was no longer on the team, the Bills have averaged six missed tackles per contest. In the six contests before the bye, Buffalo was averaging 8.5 missed tackles per game. Remember, before the spitting incident in Las Vegas, Gardner-Johnson was the owner of the highest missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties in the NFL. And don’t forget, on August 11, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said the following during a press conference on this very topic: > “Who can finish, get guys on the ground? That was an Achilles’ heel here last year. So that’s the No. 1 thing we have to correct.” Per PFF, in the regular season, the Bills averaged 8.88 missed tackles per game during the 2025 campaign. In Buffalo’s two playoff outings last season, that figure jumped to 9.5 per. Right now, even with the noticeably bad start, Buffalo’s missed tackles per game average is down to 7.5. And another strong showing in the tackling department for the Bills will go a long way in securing a win over the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, securing a 26-9 divisional victory at Highmark Stadium before turning their attention to a Thanksgiving night matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Buffalo out gained Miami 405-185, controlled the football for 36:45 and held the Dolphins to just two third down conversions on 14 attempts. Perhaps most impressive was the defense’s ability to keep Miami out of the end zone for all four quarters. There was plenty to celebrate in Buffalo’s locker room following Sunday’s victory, including a new career high for one defensive standout and another historic accomplishment for the Bills’ running back. Let’s take a look at who received game balls from head coach Joe Brady before handing out a few of our own. EDGE Greg Rousseau “Look, I could give this to everyone on defense the way y’all are playing right now,” Brady said before awarding his first game ball to Greg Rousseau. And rightfully so. Buffalo’s defense held Miami to just 185 total yards, 10 first downs and three field goals. But Rousseau finished the afternoon with three solo tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and two quarterback hits, accounting for both of Buffalo’s sacks and costing the Dolphins a combined 16 yards. His first sack came on Miami’s opening offensive possession when he brought down quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight yard loss on third and six, forcing the Dolphins to punt. With his two sack performance, Rousseau reached 10 sacks on the season, establishing a new career high with six regular season games still to play. Perhaps equally impressive is that Rousseau accomplished all of this while playing just 34 defensive snaps. RB James Cook Brady’s second game ball went to James Cook, who continues to rewrite the NFL record books. Cook finished Sunday’s contest with 22 carries for 89 yards and a touchdown. According to Brady, Cook became the first player in NFL history to record at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games. Brady also recognized Cook for reaching 1,000 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive season. And there’s still plenty of football left to be played. What continues to impress me about Cook is his consistency. Even on an afternoon when Buffalo averaged just 3.5 yards per rushing attempt as a team, Cook found a way to produce and extend his historic streak. Sara’s Game

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins 26-9 at Highmark Stadium in Week 11, putting together a dominant defensive performance just four days before they’re scheduled to host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. Buffalo’s offense accumulated 405 total yards compared to Miami’s 185, while the Bills controlled the time of possession by a margin of 13 minutes and 30 seconds. Let’s take a look at Buffalo’s Week 11 snap counts and some of the more notable personnel decisions. Buffalo controlled the clock for nearly 20 minutes in the first half alone, accumulating 254 total yards and 16 first downs while limiting Miami to just 38 yards and two first downs. Despite Buffalo’s ability to sustain drives, the offense converted just two of five red zone opportunities into touchdowns. The Bills didn’t punt once, although punter Tommy Doman contributed to the offensive production with a 30 yard completion to tight end Keleki Latu on a successful fake punt in the first quarter. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills couldn’t have asked to start Week 12 in a better position. They’re 9-1 for the first time since 1991, have the possibility of locking up the AFC East in just two weeks, and hold the cards for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. The only thing that could make things any better would be if the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos each had one more loss. But that’s okay. The Bills can take care of that themselves. sports.title: New York Jets News: Did Jets win the Aaron Rodgers Debate After Steelers Benching Decision?

AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where
sports.body: Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since 2025. Late on Tuesday, November 24 NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed “The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.” [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125442796467417433] “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career,” Pelissero added. Now feels like a perfect time to look back and judge whether the Jets made the right decision. In 2025 the Jets finished with a 3-14 record and Justin Fields delivered an uneven season before getting benched. He started nine games, completed 62.7% of his passes, threw for 1,259 passing yards, and had seven touchdowns to one interception. He also toted the rock 71 times for 383 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Pittsburgh had a 10-7 record in 2025 and made a trip to the playoffs, but ended up losing in the wildcard round. Aaron Rodgers started 16 games last season. He completed 65.7% of his passes, threw for 3,322 passing yards and had a 24 touchdown to seven interception ratio. It seems pretty obvious that Rodgers would have been a dramatic upgrade over what the Jets trotted out at QB last year. Things in 2026 feel quite the opposite. Before Rodgers got benched he started 10 games this year. He completed 60.9% of his passes, threw for 2,241 passing yards, and had a 16 touchdown to six interception ratio. The Jets are getting much better QB play than that with Geno Smith at the helm. Smith has started all 11 games so far this season. He has completed 68.1% of his passes, has thrown for 2,402 passing yards, and has a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. Seems like the Jets are better off with Smith in 2026 than Rodgers. I’m not going to pretend one win against the Chargers fundamentally changes anything. The defense is very bad from a talent standpoint and continues to perform poorly. Even against a relatively mediocre Chargers offense, there were plenty of disappointing moments. The coaching has also continued to raise legitimate concerns, particularly when it comes to clock management, situational decisions, and execution late in halves. The offensive line as a whole, David Bailey, Adonai Mitchell, and Braelon Allen are among the players who have shown signs of progress. If we look at Smith’s 2026 season in a vacuum, it is fantastic: 68.1% completion percentage, 2,402 passing yards, and a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. When you compare it to the Justin Fields experience in 2025 with the Jets? It’s almost as if the two players were competing in different sports entirely. We need to start having a real conversation about 2027. No, not tanking; let’s save that for another day. I’m talking about bringing Smith back.
